summary: Correct supporting grief-state reference from 55/22 to supplied 55/23.
rationale: The supplied token is fayəš mġammo at 55/23, while the quoted aṯi mġammo clause is independently present at 60/81. Retain the latter text and distinguish the supporting construction.

summary: Correct the supplementary mġammo reference from 55/22 to 55/23
rationale: The primary quoted sentence is correctly supported by 60/81 and is left unchanged. The supplied 55/22 contains only “W azze, mhalaxle bu darbo Ḥasan” (“und ging weiter seines Weges”), with no mġammo. The immediately following 55/23 has “Hano fayəš mġammo, daʕər laxalf”, translated “Der Mann war sehr betrübt und ging zurück”. This is the supplementary attestation of mġammo intended by the adjacent-verse reference.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC Ishaq Material culture/32)

data.translation: Are there any tragic things that happened?

rationale: First Part act. 1 example: events cause grief; -one property contrasts with an affected person mġammo.
All three Detransitive mġammo occurrences describe the affected person’s distress. Replace ambiguous causative English grievous with distressed, distinguishing active grief-causing mġammone.

summary: The supplied data distinguish grief-causing events (active Part act. mġammone) from a distressed experiencer (Detransitive Part. Pass. mġammo). This supports the existing active/Detransitive distinction, not a separate tragic-event sense.

Detransitive mġammo occurs with fayəš at 55/23, as secondary predicate with aṯi at 60/81, and with yo at 60/86. No overt agent or l-marked experiencer is present in these verses; the experiencer is the subject.
The nominal/possessive thought phrase in 60/86 provides the cause/content of distress; its durative day-and-night context is supplied by the clause, without establishing a new Infectum-wa form.

All Detransitive sources are already represented in the inherited quotation/references; only the active Part act. box receives a new example. The emotional reading gives no reason to reassign the tokens to the clouding homonym ġmm1.

Do editors intend supporting references 60/86 and 55/23 to remain attached to the short aṯi mġammo quote, or to be expanded into separate fayəš/yo examples? Their actual constructions are recorded here without duplicating evidence.
How productive is the -on- active property form mġammone outside this single attestation? Its grief-causing reading is clear, but this run does not infer additional base forms.
